title: Room booking platform: 20 rules in 4 modules
subtitle: What each rule protects, what breaks without it, and how it was checked
provenanceNote: Illustrative sample: statuses and counterexamples were written by hand to show the format; no checker was run.

modules.title: Booking
modules.summary: Request, confirm and cancel room bookings.

modules.title: Rooms & capacity
modules.summary: Match meetings to rooms that fit them.

modules.title: Approvals & access
modules.summary: Who may book, approve and change what.

rules.title: A room is never booked twice for the same time

normal.label: Normal
normal.takeaway: Room A is free from 10:00 to 11:00, so the booking is confirmed.

preview.alert: The slot is free. You can confirm the booking.

bug.label: Bug
bug.takeaway: Without the overlap check, a 10:30 booking is confirmed on top of the 10:00 meeting.

preview.alert: Confirm is still enabled although the slot overlaps.

fixed.label: Fixed
fixed.takeaway: The 30-minute overlap is caught at the gate, and 11:00 is offered instead.

preview.alert: This slot overlaps an existing booking, so Confirm is locked.

evidence.ruleSummary: Two confirmed bookings of the same room never have intersecting [start, end) intervals.
evidence.ifEnforced: Any request that overlaps an existing booking by even one minute is rejected, and the nearest free slot is suggested.
evidence.ifNotEnforced: Two teams arrive at the same room for the same meeting time.
evidence.method: Illustrative sample: written by hand to show the board format; no checker was run
evidence.sourceQuote: A room cannot be booked by two meetings at the same time.

rules.title: Bookings stay inside the building’s opening hours

normal.label: Normal
normal.takeaway: The meeting ends at 19:30, before the 20:00 close, so it is confirmed.

preview.alert: The booking fits inside opening hours.

bug.label: Bug
bug.takeaway: Only the start time is checked, so a meeting runs an hour past closing.

preview.alert: The building is locked before this meeting ends.

fixed.label: Fixed
fixed.takeaway: The whole interval must fit inside opening hours, so the request is rejected.

preview.alert: Pick a slot that ends by 20:00.

evidence.ruleSummary: Every confirmed booking starts at or after opening time and ends at or before closing time.
evidence.ifEnforced: Requests that run past closing time are rejected with the opening hours shown.
evidence.ifNotEnforced: Meetings are confirmed in a building that is locked before they end.
evidence.method: Illustrative sample: written by hand to show the board format; no checker was run

rules.title: Cancelling a booking frees its slot at once

normal.label: Normal
normal.takeaway: Cancelling booking #812 releases the 14:00 slot for others.

preview.alert: The slot is available again.

bug.label: Bug
bug.takeaway: Only the status changes, so the slot stays reserved by a cancelled booking.

preview.alert: The calendar shows the room as busy forever.

fixed.label: Fixed
fixed.takeaway: Status and slot change in one step, so the slot is free as soon as the cancel commits.

preview.alert: The slot is free in the same step as the cancel.

evidence.ruleSummary: After a booking is cancelled, its slot is eventually free, and no cancelled booking holds a slot.
evidence.ifEnforced: A cancelled meeting gives its room back immediately.
evidence.ifNotEnforced: Cancelled meetings keep rooms blocked and the calendar fills with ghost reservations.
evidence.method: Illustrative sample: written by hand to show the board format; no checker was run

rules.title: Only verified accounts can book rooms

normal.label: Normal
normal.takeaway: Dana has a verified account, so the booking goes through.

preview.alert: Your booking is confirmed.

bug.label: Bug
bug.takeaway: A freshly created, unverified account books the boardroom.

preview.alert: Anyone with a new account can hold rooms.

fixed.label: Fixed
fixed.takeaway: Unverified accounts are asked to verify their email before booking.

preview.alert: Verify your email address to book rooms.

evidence.ruleSummary: Every confirmed booking belongs to an account whose email is verified.
evidence.ifEnforced: Unverified accounts cannot hold rooms.
evidence.ifNotEnforced: Throwaway accounts can reserve rooms and block real teams.
evidence.method: Illustrative sample: written by hand to show the board format; no checker was run

rules.title: Recurring series skip public holidays

normal.label: Normal
normal.takeaway: An ordinary Monday gets its weekly occurrence.

preview.alert: The occurrence is on the calendar.

bug.label: Bug
bug.takeaway: The series ignores the holiday calendar and books the room on a public holiday.

preview.alert: Facilities staff open the building for nobody.

fixed.label: Fixed
fixed.takeaway: Holiday dates are skipped and the series continues the following week.

preview.alert: This date is a public holiday, so it was skipped.

evidence.ruleSummary: No occurrence of a recurring series falls on a date in the holiday calendar.
evidence.ifEnforced: Series silently skip holidays and resume afterwards.
evidence.ifNotEnforced: Rooms are booked on days the building is closed.
evidence.method: Illustrative sample: written by hand to show the board format; no checker was run

rules.title: Attendees never exceed the room’s capacity

normal.label: Normal
normal.takeaway: Eight attendees in an eight-seat room is exactly at capacity, so it is accepted.

preview.alert: Everyone fits.

bug.label: Bug
bug.takeaway: The invite list grows to eleven in a room with eight seats.

preview.alert: Three people will be standing.

fixed.label: Fixed
fixed.takeaway: The capacity check stops the list at eight and suggests a twelve-seat room.

preview.alert: Move to Room C (12 seats) to invite everyone.

evidence.ruleSummary: For every confirmed booking, the number of attendees is at most the room’s seat count.
evidence.ifEnforced: Large meetings are steered to rooms that fit them.
evidence.ifNotEnforced: Meetings are overbooked and people stand or leave.
evidence.method: Illustrative sample: written by hand to show the board format; no checker was run

rules.title: Rooms booked for video calls have a camera

normal.label: Normal
normal.takeaway: Room B has a camera, so it is offered for the video call.

preview.alert: Room B has everything this meeting needs.

bug.label: Bug
bug.takeaway: A room without a camera is offered for a video call.

preview.alert: The call starts in a room that cannot join it.

fixed.label: Fixed
fixed.takeaway: Rooms that lack required equipment are not offered.

preview.alert: Only rooms with a camera are shown.

evidence.ruleSummary: Every offered room has all equipment the meeting requires.
evidence.ifEnforced: People never land in a room that cannot run their meeting.
evidence.ifNotEnforced: Video calls start in rooms without cameras.
evidence.method: Illustrative sample: written by hand to show the board format; no checker was run

rules.title: Rooms under maintenance cannot be booked

normal.label: Normal
normal.takeaway: No maintenance is planned on Tuesday, so the booking is confirmed.

preview.alert: Room C is available.

bug.label: Bug
bug.takeaway: Only other bookings are checked, so the room is booked while it is being repaired.

preview.alert: The meeting collides with the repair crew.

fixed.label: Fixed
fixed.takeaway: Maintenance windows block bookings just like other meetings.

preview.alert: Room C is closed for maintenance at that time.

evidence.ruleSummary: No confirmed booking intersects a maintenance window of the same room.
evidence.ifEnforced: Repair work and meetings never share a room.
evidence.ifNotEnforced: People arrive to a room full of ladders.
evidence.method: Illustrative sample: written by hand to show the board format; no checker was run

rules.title: Step-free meetings only get step-free rooms

normal.label: Normal
normal.takeaway: Room A has lift access, so it is offered.

preview.alert: This room has step-free access.

bug.label: Bug
bug.takeaway: A mezzanine room with stairs only is offered to a step-free meeting.

preview.alert: An attendee cannot reach the room.

fixed.label: Fixed
fixed.takeaway: Rooms without step-free access are hidden for these meetings.

preview.alert: Only step-free rooms are shown.

evidence.ruleSummary: If a meeting requires step-free access, every room offered for it has step-free access.
evidence.ifEnforced: Every attendee can reach the room.
evidence.ifNotEnforced: Attendees who need step-free access are excluded.
evidence.method: Illustrative sample: written by hand to show the board format; no checker was run

rules.title: Large rooms keep a 15-minute cleaning gap

normal.label: Normal
normal.takeaway: A 15-minute gap after the previous meeting leaves time to clean.

preview.alert: Cleaning fits between the meetings.

bug.label: Bug
bug.takeaway: Back-to-back bookings are allowed in the hall, leaving no time to clean it.

preview.alert: The next meeting starts in an uncleaned hall.

fixed.label: Fixed
fixed.takeaway: The booking is shifted to 12:15 to keep the cleaning gap.

preview.alert: We moved your start to 12:15 to keep the cleaning gap.

evidence.ruleSummary: For rooms with 20 or more seats, consecutive bookings are at least 15 minutes apart.
evidence.ifEnforced: Large rooms are always cleaned between meetings.
evidence.ifNotEnforced: Back-to-back events start in a messy room.
evidence.method: Illustrative sample: written by hand to show the board format; no checker was run
evidence.counterexample:
State 1: book(Hall, 11:00, 12:00) -> confirmed
State 2: book(Hall, 12:00, 13:00) -> confirmed
State 3: gap(Hall) = 0 min
State 4: CleaningGapKept = false

rules.title: The boardroom needs manager approval

normal.label: Normal
normal.takeaway: Kim approved the request, so the boardroom is booked.

preview.alert: Approved and confirmed.

bug.label: Bug
bug.takeaway: The booking is confirmed while the approval is still pending.

preview.alert: Executives find their room taken by an unapproved meeting.

fixed.label: Fixed
fixed.takeaway: The request waits until a manager approves it.

preview.alert: Waiting for Kim to approve.

evidence.ruleSummary: A boardroom booking is confirmed only after a manager approves it.
evidence.ifEnforced: The boardroom is used only for approved meetings.
evidence.ifNotEnforced: Anyone can take the boardroom without asking.
evidence.method: Illustrative sample: written by hand to show the board format; no checker was run

rules.title: Only the organizer can change a booking

normal.label: Normal
normal.takeaway: Ana organizes the meeting, so her change is saved.

preview.alert: Your changes are saved.

bug.label: Bug
bug.takeaway: Any attendee can move or shorten someone else’s meeting.

preview.alert: Ana’s meeting was moved without her knowing.

fixed.label: Fixed
fixed.takeaway: Only the organizer, or an assistant they named, can change the booking.

preview.alert: Only Ana can change this booking.

evidence.ruleSummary: A booking is modified only by its organizer or a delegate the organizer named.
evidence.ifEnforced: Meetings change only when their owner says so.
evidence.ifNotEnforced: Attendees silently move each other’s meetings.
evidence.method: Illustrative sample: written by hand to show the board format; no checker was run

rules.title: Approvals expire after 24 hours

normal.label: Normal
normal.takeaway: The approval is 23 hours old, so it can still be used.

preview.alert: Approval is still valid.

bug.label: Bug
bug.takeaway: An approval from Monday is used to confirm a booking on Friday.

preview.alert: The manager approved a different plan days ago.

fixed.label: Fixed
fixed.takeaway: Approvals older than 24 hours must be requested again.

preview.alert: This approval expired. Ask your manager again.

evidence.ruleSummary: A booking is confirmed only with an approval younger than 24 hours.
evidence.ifEnforced: Approvals reflect the current plan.
evidence.ifNotEnforced: Old approvals are reused for changed plans.
evidence.method: Illustrative sample: written by hand to show the board format; no checker was run

rules.title: Assistants book only for people who named them

normal.label: Normal
normal.takeaway: Kim named Lee as an assistant, so Lee books on Kim’s behalf.

preview.alert: Booked on behalf of Kim.

bug.label: Bug
bug.takeaway: Lee books rooms in Raj’s name without Raj delegating anything.

preview.alert: Raj is shown as the organizer of a meeting he never made.

fixed.label: Fixed
fixed.takeaway: Booking on behalf of someone requires their delegation.

preview.alert: Raj has not named you as an assistant.

evidence.ruleSummary: A booking made on behalf of a user exists only if that user delegated to the booker.
evidence.ifEnforced: Nobody books in another person’s name without consent.
evidence.ifNotEnforced: Assistants can impersonate anyone.
evidence.method: Illustrative sample: written by hand to show the board format; no checker was run

rules.title: Guest badges are issued only for confirmed bookings

normal.label: Normal
normal.takeaway: Sam’s host has a confirmed booking, so the badge is printed.

preview.alert: Badge printed for Sam.

bug.label: Bug
bug.takeaway: Badges are printed even after the host cancelled the booking.

preview.alert: A guest walks in with no meeting to attend.

fixed.label: Fixed
fixed.takeaway: Reception calls the host when there is no confirmed booking.

preview.alert: No confirmed booking. Please call the host.

evidence.ruleSummary: A guest badge is issued only while its host booking is confirmed.
evidence.ifEnforced: Guests are admitted only for real meetings.
evidence.ifNotEnforced: Badges are handed out for cancelled meetings.
evidence.method: Illustrative sample: written by hand to show the board format; no checker was run

rules.title: Each paid booking is charged exactly once

normal.label: Normal
normal.takeaway: The first charge for booking #4410 goes through.

preview.alert: Paid: $40.

bug.label: Bug
bug.takeaway: A network retry charges the card a second time.

preview.alert: The customer was charged twice.

fixed.label: Fixed
fixed.takeaway: The retry carries the same key and returns the original charge.

preview.alert: Already paid. No second charge.

evidence.ruleSummary: For every booking, the number of successful charges is at most one.
evidence.ifEnforced: Retries and double clicks never cost the customer twice.
evidence.ifNotEnforced: Flaky networks turn into duplicate charges and refunds.
evidence.scope: 2 bookings, up to 3 retries, 1 network drop
evidence.method: Illustrative sample: written by hand to show the board format; no checker was run

rules.title: Team bookings stay within the monthly budget

normal.label: Normal
normal.takeaway: The booking costs $120 and the team has $300 left this month.

preview.alert: Within budget.

bug.label: Bug
bug.takeaway: A $450 event is confirmed and pushes the team over its monthly budget.

preview.alert: Finance sees an overspend at month end.

fixed.label: Fixed
fixed.takeaway: Bookings that would exceed the budget wait for a finance approval.

preview.alert: This booking needs finance approval.

evidence.ruleSummary: The sum of a team’s confirmed paid bookings in a month never exceeds its budget without approval.
evidence.ifEnforced: Overspending needs an explicit approval.
evidence.ifNotEnforced: Budgets are discovered to be blown only at month end.
evidence.method: Illustrative sample: written by hand to show the board format; no checker was run

rules.title: Calendar sync never overwrites a newer change

normal.label: Normal
normal.takeaway: The incoming change is based on the stored version, so it is applied.

preview.alert: Calendars are in sync.

bug.label: Bug
bug.takeaway: A stale sync silently overwrites a newer change made in the app.

preview.alert: The organizer’s new time is silently reverted.

fixed.label: Fixed
fixed.takeaway: Stale updates get 409 Conflict and the sync fetches the latest version first.

preview.alert: Conflict detected. Fetching the latest version.

evidence.ruleSummary: An update is applied only if it was based on the latest stored version.
evidence.ifEnforced: Two-way sync never loses an edit.
evidence.ifNotEnforced: Edits made in one place vanish when the other syncs.
evidence.method: Illustrative sample: written by hand to show the board format; no checker was run

rules.title: Unclaimed rooms are released after 15 minutes

normal.label: Normal
normal.takeaway: The organizer checks in within 15 minutes, so the room is kept.

preview.alert: Checked in.

bug.label: Bug
bug.takeaway: Nobody shows up and the room stays reserved and empty for an hour.

preview.alert: Others cannot use a room that nobody is in.

fixed.label: Fixed
fixed.takeaway: Without a check-in by 10:15 the room is released for others.

preview.alert: No check-in, so the room was released at 10:15.

evidence.ruleSummary: A booking without check-in is eventually released, at most 15 minutes after its start.
evidence.ifEnforced: No-shows do not waste rooms.
evidence.ifNotEnforced: Rooms sit empty while others search for space.
evidence.method: Illustrative sample: written by hand to show the board format; no checker was run

rules.title: Refunds never exceed what was charged

normal.label: Normal
normal.takeaway: A full refund of the $40 charge is allowed.

preview.alert: Refund issued.

bug.label: Bug
bug.takeaway: A second full refund is issued for the same charge.

preview.alert: The company pays the customer twice.

fixed.label: Fixed
fixed.takeaway: The refund total is capped at the original charge.

preview.alert: This charge is already fully refunded.

evidence.ruleSummary: For every charge, the total refunded is at most the amount charged.
evidence.ifEnforced: Refunds can never create money.
evidence.ifNotEnforced: Duplicate refunds drain revenue.
evidence.method: Illustrative sample: written by hand to show the board format; no checker was run
